nodes.name: Electrochemical Exfoliation
nodes.procedure: EG was obtained by electrochemical exfoliation treatment of graphite foil in 0.1 M (NH4)2SO4 solution.
nodes.source_text: EG, which was obtained by electrochemical exfoliation treatment of graphite foil in 0.1 M (NH4)2SO4 solution.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Co(OH)2 Nanosheet Array
nodes.procedure: The Co(OH)2 nanosheet array was directly electrodeposited onto the surface of EG, which was obtained by electrochemical exfoliation treatment of graphite foil in 0.1 M (NH4)2SO4 solution.
nodes.source_text: The Co(OH)2 nanosheet array was directly electrodeposited onto the surface of EG, which was obtained by electrochemical exfoliation treatment of graphite foil in 0.1 M (NH4)2SO4 solution.

nodes.name: Vapor-phase Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: The resulting EG/Co(OH)2 was converted into EG/Co(OH)2/ZIF-67 via a vapor-phase hydrothermal reaction with 2-methylimidazole vapor. Optimal reaction time of 15 min was identified.

unit_operations.name: Vapor-phase Hydrothermal Reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: vapor-phase hydrothermal reaction with 2-methylimidazole vapor... optimal time of 15 min

nodes.source_text: The resulting EG/Co(OH)2 was converted into EG/Co(OH)2/ZIF-67 via a vapor-phase hydrothermal reaction with 2-methylimidazole vapor. We systematically explored the influence of different reaction times (5, 10, 15, 20, 30, and 40 min) and the optimal time of 15 min was identified.

nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic activity... was evaluated in 1.0 M KOH solution via a typical three-electrode system. All potentials were converted to the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE)... EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid exhibits the best OER performance with a low overpotential of 280 mV to drive a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope of 63 mV dec⁻¹... current density of... 55 mA cm⁻² at 1.6 V... Cdl value of 91.4 mF cm⁻²... almost no decrease in the current density... after 10 h... no significant increase... after 1000 cycles.

The overpotential of 280 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² for EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 is much lower than that of the commercial Ir/C catalyst 340 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²... a low Tafel slope of 63 mV dec⁻¹... for commercial Ir/C, 80 mV dec⁻¹... Ir/C (25.4 mA cm⁻²)

nodes.description: Multi-current step OER test in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The multi-current step curve was measured... With the current density increasing from 10 to 100 mA cm⁻², the potential could not only swiftly respond to the change of current density, but also stay at a constant value for 5000 s.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows vertical Co(OH)₂ nanosheet array with average thickness of ~10 nm on EG, increasing to ~20 nm after ZIF-67 coating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the FESEM image of EG/Co(OH)₂ showed a vertical and uniform Co(OH)₂ nanosheet array with an average thickness of ~10 nm deposited on the surface of EG. After further treatment with 2-methylimidazole vapor, the thickness of the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid was increased to ~20 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms ultrathin ZIF-67 nanosheet thickness of around 6 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and corresponding height distribution showed that the thickness of the ultrathin ZIF-67 nanosheets was around 6 nm, consistent with the FESEM measurement

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX and elemental mapping confirm presence of Co, N, and O elements in EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectrum (EDX) and elemental mapping results revealed the existence of Co, N and O elements in the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals layer structure of EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid is shown in Fig. 2c, from which the layer structure was clearly observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.159, 0.178, and 0.240 nm corresponding to (110), (102), and (101) planes of Co(OH)₂; ZIF-67 shows amorphous characteristics without observable lattice fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images showed the spatial distribution of the ultrathin ZIF-67 and Co(OH)₂ nanosheet array. Closer observations revealed that a close interfacial contact was formed between the inner dark area with lattice fringe spacings of 0.159, 0.178 and 0.240 nm, associated with the (110), (102) and (101) planes of Co(OH)₂ nanosheets, and the outer light area without observable lattice fringes of ZIF-67

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid indexed to crystal planes of Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid can be well indexed to the crystal planes of Co(OH)₂

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD peaks at 19.0°, 37.0°, and 51.4° indexed to (001), (102), and (110) planes of Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD diffraction peaks observed at 19.0, 37.0, and 51.4° for the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 were well indexed to the (001), (102), and (110) crystal planes of Co(OH)₂

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR confirms presence of ZIF-67 by characteristic peaks in 500-4000 cm⁻¹ region.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of ZIF-67 in the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 was confirmed by the FTIR spectra, which showed the characteristic diffraction peaks of ZIF-67 in the 500-4000 cm⁻¹ region

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks at 518 cm⁻¹ (Co–O stretching of Co(OH)₂) and 426 cm⁻¹ (Co–N stretching of ZIF-67) confirm coexistence of both components.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 contained several typical peaks from 235 to 765 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the Co(OH)₂ and ZIF-67. For example, the peaks at 518 and 426 cm⁻¹ can be indexed to the Co–O stretching of Co(OH)₂ and Co–N stretching of ZIF-67, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms Co, N, O elements; C 1s peaks at 284.2, 284.9, 286.0, 291.4 eV for C–C, C–N, C=N, O=C–O; N 1s shows down-shift indicating electronic interaction; Co 2p shows 1.2 eV decrease due to electron transfer from ZIF-67 to Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey spectrum of EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 provided solid evidence for the existence Co, N, and O elements. The high-resolution C 1s spectrum can be deconvoluted into four peaks centred at 284.2, 284.9, 286.0, and 291.4 eV, which are attributed to C–C, C–N, C=N, and O=C–O groups

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman under OER conditions shows Co–O peaks at 455 and 522 cm⁻¹ at 1.4 V shifting to 465 and 526 cm⁻¹ at 2.0 V with increased intensity, indicating transformation of Co–O species into Co–OOH active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Co–O peaks were located at 455 and 522 cm⁻¹ at a potential of 1.4 V, while the Co–O peaks were up-shifted to 465 and 526 cm⁻¹ when the applied potential was increased to 2.0 V. During this OER process, it can be noticed that the intensity of Co–O peaks increased with increasing the reaction potential, which can be due to the transformation of the Co–O species into Co–OOH groups

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl = 91.4 mF cm⁻² for EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67, indicating highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the EG/Co(OH)₂/ZIF-67 hybrid possessed the highest C_dl value of 91.4 mF cm⁻² compared to EG/Co(OH)₂ (86.6 mF cm⁻²) and EG/ZIF-67 (73.4 mF cm⁻²)
